sentences.text: If your engine quits a mile off the beach with the wind blowing onshore, one piece of gear stands between you and the surf.
It’s safety equipment first, and a fishing tool second.
Look at the four types on screen.
A fluke anchor, often called a Danforth, is light, stows flat, and holds very well in sand and mud.
That’s why you’ll see it on nearly every Florida fishing boat.
Its weakness is grass and rock.
A plow or claw holds in most bottoms, and resets itself if the wind shifts.
A mushroom anchor works by suction in soft mud, and it’s for permanent moorings.
And a grapnel hooks into rocks and wrecks.
It’s popular for fishing structure, but it fouls easily, so rig it to break free.
So which one for a sandy bottom off Clearwater?
Match the anchor to the bottom.
